name: High-rise tailored trousers
lead: High-rise tailored trousers sit at or above the natural waist and are hemmed to a clean length. In height and proportion discussions, proponents say they raise the visual waistline and so make the legs look longer relative to the torso.
Trousers are commonly hemmed to adjust leg length, and higher-quality pairs may leave extra seam allowance at the centre back for adjusting the waist.[1]
No studies of trouser rise and perceived leg length were found in this entry's sources.

paras: Tailors hem trouser legs to prevent fraying and set length, and waists can be adjusted within limits.[1] Rise refers to where the waistband sits; proponents of high rise say a higher waistband shifts the apparent leg-to-torso split upward.

card.summary: Higher waistband plus a tailored hem, said to lengthen the leg line; unstudied.
card.note: Perceived-height effect not tested in the sources.

quick.overview:
High-rise trousers with tailored hems are claimed to make legs look longer.

The idea is part of proportion-focused style advice.
quick.mechanism: A higher waistband raises the visible waistline, so legs occupy more of the figure.
quick.risks: Low risk. No studies on the effect were found.
